info.title: Spike Statements API
info.description:
# Introduction

Spike offers a number of APIs that provide open-banking equivalent capabilities for South African banks like ABSA, Capitec, FNB, Nedbank, RMB, and Standard Bank.

The Spike Statements API provides you with capabilities to extract data from pdf bank statements. Pdfs are [difficult](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/articles/why-pdfs-are-hard-to-process/) for machines to process. Spike solves this problem by extracting structured data from a pdf - data like transactions, and account holder info.

This API allows you to integrate statement processing capabilities directly into your own software. If you simply need to extract transactions from a pdf into excel then you can use our online [pdf converter](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/user-guides/app/web-converter/) without needing to write any code.

Statement processing is used by our clients to assist with accounting, lending, and personal financial management operations.

This guide is part of a suite of [technical resources](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/#api-resources) which we provide in order to help developers make use of the Spike API.

## Table of contents

To get you up to speed with the Spike Statements API we provide the following resources:

- [Postman extensions](#postman-extensions)
  - we've used various tricks in order to help you get the most out of postman
- [Specifications](#specifications)
  - We provide technical specifications for all endpoints using the two most widely adopted REST-ful API definition systems: [openapi](https://swagger.io/specification/) and [postman](https://www.postman.com/)
- [Developer guide](#developer-guide)
  - These guides provide guided walkthroughs and overviews of important features and concepts
- [Errors](#errors)
  - A note on the manner in which errors are returned by the Spike API
- [Libraries](#libraries)
  - For those that want type safety and other embellishments we support a range of language specific libraries to access the Spike API. This is entirely optional.
- [Samples](#samples)
  - For those who like to learn by doing we provide full-source code for a range of sample applications that make use of the Spike API.
- [Support](#support)
  - If you get stuck we're on hand to assist
- [Testing sandbox](#testing-sandbox)
  - To query the Spike API during testing.

## Postman

See our [postman article](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/articles/postman/) for a number of tricks and techniques which will help you get the most out of this postman collection.

For example - here's how you can enter the required inputs for the `/pdf` function:

```sh
# file
base64 -w 0 /path/to/your.pdf | xclip -selection clipboard
# the base64 pdf has been copied to your clipboard - you can now paste it into the appropriate parameter or body in Postman

# token
cat /path/to/your/token | xclip -selection clipboard
# the token has been copied to your clipboard - you can now paste it into the appropriate authorization parameter in Postman
```

## Specifications

We provide technical specifications for all endpoints using the two most widely adopted REST-ful API definition systems:

### OpenApi

[OpenApi](https://swagger.io/specification/) (formerly Swagger) defines all inputs and outputs from each function[^diff] along with examples of these inputs and outputs. Each function definition is contained within a single .json (or .yaml) file. This json can be used for automatic client code generation but this is typically overkill, it's primarily useful as a reference document (e.g. to see all possible response shapes and to define any enumeration values).

[^diff]: OpenApi differs from Postman - there is a definition file **per-function** whereas Postman has a definition for a **collection** of related functions.

See the [openapi specs](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/api/) on the Spike Documentation site.

### Postman

The guide that you are currently reading.

## Developer guide

The [quick start for new developers](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/developer-guide/quick-start-for-new-devs/README.md) provides the shortest path to getting up and running for new devs.

Our full [developer guide](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/developer-guide/) provides guided walkthroughs of how to make a request and how to process the response - as well as guides to describe features like [authenticity](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/product/authenticity/)

**NOTE:** The specs are updated by an automated process from the source code and hence are the most accurate. If there is a discrepancy between the developer guide and the specs, then consider the specs to be the authoritative source.

## Authorization

Before you make a query to the Spike API you will need an API token. See the [authorization guide](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/developer-guide/authorization/).

**WARNING**: Never share your tokens with anyone. If your token is used to query the Spike API then this will be billed to your account.

## Errors

Spike returns json objects for all responses. We do not use http status codes - all responses successes and errors will be `HTTP Status Code 200`. The way that you distinguish a success response from an error response is via `.type` field in the response object.

There are some cases where you will see a non-200 http status code. This includes all normal network connectivity issues (like `401 Unauthorized`, `408 Request Timeout`, `522 Connection Timed Out` etc...) which prevent the request from being received by Spike, or when your request triggers an underlying restriction that is imposed by the cloud hosting infrastructure upon which we host our service. We highlight the following http errors:

| http status code | http status text      | when it may occur                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 413              | Payload too large     | You may see this error if you attempt to upload a very large pdf. This limit comes from our hosting provider: the [maximum payload size](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html) for an AWS Lambda request is 6MB. |
| 500              | Internal Server Error | This is very rare. It would indicate an unhandled exception on our servers. Please report this using the [support](#support) channel below.                                                                                                         |

## Libraries

In order to provide a quicker more typesafe path for developers to make use of the Spike API, we have developed request wrapper libraries for specific programming languages.

Using our libraries is entirely optional - you're free to use any request library (e.g. axios, request, node-fetch) that you like and manually construct the request payload yourself.

See the list of [officially supported languages](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/developer-guide/libs/).

## Samples

Spike provides various sample apps which you can use as demonstrations of how to use the Spike API. These can all be found in the [samples repo](https://github.com/spikedata/samples). See the README in that repo for a table of samples.

## Support

Please see the [support guide](https://docs.spikedata.co.za/product/support/) to find out how to contact us.

## Testing sandbox

Spike provides a test endpoint `/pdf2test`:

- this accepts the same inputs as the `/pdf2` endpoint but is free to use
- it is limited in the following ways: (1) it only returns the first 10 transactions in each pdf (2) it is not monitored by our support system

Note: the sandbox response is limited in various ways in order to ensure that it is not used by production code.
